newsitem.title: GERMANY: German court rules against Kirch's DF1.
newsitem.headline: German court rules against Kirch's DF1.

text.p: Germany's digital television war took another turn on Wednesday when a Hamburg court ruled that Bavarian media mogul Leo Kirch's digital pay TV channel DF1 has no licence to sell programming outside of Bavaria.

DF1 immediately launched an appeal against the ruling and the Bavarian media regulatory agency issued a statement in support of the station, saying the Hamburg court had "falsely interpreted" its broadcasting licence.

The court ruling was in response to a suit filed by DF1 competitor Premiere, which alleged that DF1 had an unfair advantage because it was broadcasting and marketing its service nationally although its licence restricted it to Bavaria.
"With this decision, the Hamburg state court has eliminated DF1's unfair competitive advantage," said Premiere Managing Director Bernd Kundrun in a statement.
The battle between Premiere and DF1 is a strange corporate conflict that has Kirch, a Premiere shareholder, at odds with the station he helped to build.

Leo Kirch holds a stake of 25 percent in Premiere, but has been trying for over a year to prevent it from offering digital pay TV services. Instead, he wants his DF1 to become the main platform for digital television in Germany.
But Premiere's other shareholders, Bertelsmann AG and French pay TV group Canal Plus, want Premiere to become the main digital TV outlet.
The two sides have been trying for months to reach a compromise and industry observers believe that at some point they will reach an agreement that somehow integrates the two channels.
While Premiere may have won a symbolic victory in the Hamburg court, Bavarian media regulators said they expected DF1 to eventually win during the appeal process.
The regulator issued an additional order supplementary to the licence to make clear that DF1 may broadcast nationally.
"The president of the media regulatory office, Prof. Dr. Wolf-Dieter Ring, expects that DF1 will be exonerated in a further hearing as a result of this order," the regulator said in a statement.
DF1 officials appeared relaxed and said the decision would have little impact on their business and said Premiere was taking sides with its shareholder Bertelsmann against Kirch.
"The impression is growing in the industry that someone is trying to achieve in court what they have not been able to achieve in the market," said Kirch Group managing director Gottfried Zmeck.

Premiere is Germany's largest pay television channel with more than 1.41 million subscribers. It currently offers analogue programming and will soon launch a digital television pilot project with 30,000 subscribers.
DF1, which began broadcasting in July, has won around 20,000 subscribers.
